questions.stem: The 'BRICS' grouping originally comprised five countries. The 'S' stands for:
questions.explanation: BRIC (2006) — Brazil, Russia, India, China — became BRICS in 2010 with the addition of South Africa. The group is expanding — as of 1 January 2024, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the UAE joined; Saudi Arabia has been formally invited, Argentina declined. The New Development Bank (NDB) is headquartered in Shanghai.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a member of OPEC (Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries)?
questions.explanation: OPEC — 13 founding / continuing members (as of 2024) — Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Venezuela (founding 5, 1960) + Algeria, Libya, Nigeria, UAE, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea, Congo, and others. India is a net oil importer, not a producer-exporter of any scale — and not an OPEC member. OPEC+ (since 2016) is a broader grouping that includes Russia, Kazakhstan, Mexico and others.

questions.stem: The G20 presidency for 2023 was held by India. Which member's flag was the backdrop of the New Delhi summit's logo design?
questions.explanation: The 2023 G20 India presidency logo incorporated the lotus — the national flower. Theme — 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' / 'One Earth, One Family, One Future'. At the New Delhi summit (September 2023), the African Union was admitted as the 21st permanent member. India passed the presidency to Brazil for 2024. The G20 includes the G7, BRICS and most major economies.

questions.stem: NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation) was founded in which year in response to the Cold War?
questions.explanation: NATO was established on 4 April 1949 by the North Atlantic Treaty (Washington Treaty). Originally 12 members; now 32 (Finland joined 2023, Sweden 2024). HQed in Brussels. Core principle — Article 5, collective defence (an attack on one is an attack on all), invoked only once (after 9/11, 2001). Warsaw Pact (the Soviet-led counter) was founded in 1955 and dissolved in 1991.

questions.stem: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) comprises how many member states?
questions.explanation: ASEAN — 10 members: Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam. Founded 1967 (Bangkok Declaration) by 5 founding members. Secretariat in Jakarta. Timor-Leste has been an observer since 2022 (with full admission anticipated). India is a dialogue partner + 'Act East Policy' and participates in ASEAN-led forums like the East Asia Summit.

questions.stem: India is a founding member of which regional economic grouping formed in 1985?
questions.explanation: SAARC — 8 member states (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Maldives + Afghanistan since 2007). Founded in Dhaka, 8 December 1985; secretariat in Kathmandu. Despite initial hopes, SAARC has been hobbled by India-Pakistan tensions — no summit has been held since Kathmandu 2014. India's alternative focus has increasingly been on BIMSTEC (India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand) — excluding Pakistan.

questions.stem: The European Union (EU) currently has how many member states?
questions.explanation: EU — 27 members. The UK formally left the EU on 31 January 2020 (Brexit), reducing the membership from 28 to 27. Croatia was the latest to join (2013). HQ — Brussels. Common currency — the Euro (€), shared by 20 of the 27 members (the 'Eurozone'). Schengen area (free movement) is a related but distinct overlapping grouping.
